So I got a new Neon Blue Dwarf Guorami 3 days ago. I have an established community 20 gallon tank with the world's most timid dwarf puffer, 5 neon tetras, and 5 dwarf chain loaches. Well, it used to be 5 neons, now it's 4, thanks to Mr. Murder the Gourami. With the new fish, capacity is 98% full, and not entirely since a few fish are still juveniles.

Various low light plants, annubius, java ferns, cryptocornes, amazon swords, african water fern. Lots of slate slabs making a giant pile of caves in the corner. The light generally stays off since most of my fish don't like it. Filtration is 400%.

My most recent test showed Nitrates 50 / Nitrites 0 / PH 7.8 / KH 10 / GH >16 which is typical.

So Mr. Murder took to chasing the tetras the second he entered the tank. After a couple minutes, he calmed down, explored a bit, and settled in. On day 2 he started nipping at the tetras. And then the loaches. And then the puffer. So all of the fish, including the puffer, just swam away from him.

Over the course of the day Mr. Murder would randomly chase all the fish, and nip at their tails. They were all terrified and hiding, except for the loaches, who kept grouping up and chasing him out of their cave.

He swam to and fro throughout the whole tank, in and out of the loach cave, the puffer's favorite plant, and the tetra's middle open area. I floated some plants up in the corner for him, away from the other fish, but it only distracted him shortly before he returned to swimming the whole tank. He didn't just want a corner or the plants he'd slept in the night before- he wanted the whole tank.

On day 3 one of my first fish, a neon tetra, was missing half his tail fin. The whole top half was missing. While I contemplated what to do, Mr. Murder gave chase to him again, and he hid in a plant where he died.

It is possible, but entirely unlikely, that the puffer nipped the fin. I didn't see it happen. I've had this puffer from a juvenile and he's never nipped or chased the other fish. The tetras steal worms out of his mouth all the time, and he doesn't even react to that. I've never seen a nipped fin until Mr. Murder came along. And puffpuff was just as terrified of him as the others. I did see some serious nips coming from Mr. Murder, and although one tail bite caused a tetra to jump out of the water, I didn't see the actual nip that took the tetra's fin.

Mr. Murder is currently in solitary confinement, in a little 3 gallon nano tank, while I figure out what to do with him.

Should I give him another chance, re-arrange the tank and try again? Or return him to the store immediately? I was hoping he'd cool down in the nano but so far he's just been attacking his reflection. He's a juvenile. I want to give him another chance, it was only his 3rd day, but my current fish are so scared that they wouldn't even come out to eat for fear he might turn up today (he was in the habit of chasing them all off during feeding time). The puffer's just been curling his tail and acting skittish, and the tetras are in disarray and sparring one another now that the only male tetra is gone.

2nd chance or return?

Here is a picture of Mr. Murder in his solitary confinement tank, if you're curious:

http://i.imgur.com/lYCfvwo.jpg

EDIT: In case anyone with the same problem ever reads this, the plan worked! The fish calmed down while in solitary, and I rearranged the main tank and created some new caves right before putting him back in. He promptly claimed a fresh cave and stopped attacking the other fish.
What to do with new, murdering dwarf gourami?

Gourami's are considered semi aggressive, and they will attack small fish for terrority, but if you have fish the same size or bigger they usually leave them alone from what I have seen in my experiences with them. and honestly he looks really good in that 3 gallon nano, I'd leave him there in time out, I think he'd like that better, and will probably have both tanks happy, hope that helped, and good luck with Mr. Murder.

Ha, yea I posted that a couple days ago, and since then he really chilled out in the nano and started behaving like a normal fish. So today I threw him back in the main tank. I totally rearranged it and took apart the old cave system and build a separate little cave for him in the front corner. I redirected the filter non return valve above the water with suction cups, so now there's no current there and it's unclaimed territory. So far so good, he's taken to the new cave and is only chasing others away when they swim too close. Still early days though... He is by far the biggest fish in the tank so I hope he settles his territory and calms the hell down, otherwise it's back to solitary!

Here's some pics of the new set up, :-)

Awesome glad it worked out, and the tank looks like a great setup!
